title: Accounts and the sandbox
intro: This section is about everyone who uses the platform, whatever their organisation. It covers getting in (sign in, sign up, password reset, invites), moving between the sample accounts, resetting the sandbox, and the tools that work on every page: search, undo, and the pages shown when something cannot be opened. Everything runs in the person's own browser as a sandbox, no email is ever sent, and steps anyone can take are drawn in plain white boxes.

workflows.title: Sign in and return to the page you asked for
workflows.where: Sign in page (/signin), reached from the landing page or by opening any /app address while signed out
workflows.summary: A person signs in with their email and password, or with one click on a sample account card. If they were sent to sign in from a page inside the app, they land back on that page; otherwise they land on their home page.
workflows.mermaid:
flowchart TD
A["Opens a page inside the app"] --> B{"Signed in?"}:::system
B -->|"Yes"| C(["Page opens"])
B -->|"No"| D["Sent to Sign in, page remembered"]:::system
S["Opens Sign in from the landing page"] --> E
D --> E{"Use a sample account?"}
E -->|"Yes"| F["Clicks a sample account card"]
E -->|"No"| G["Enters email and password, presses Sign in"]
F --> H{"Email and password match?"}:::system
G --> H
H -->|"No"| I(["That email and password do not match"]):::system
H -->|"Yes"| J["Signed in"]:::system
J --> K(["Page asked for opens, or home"])

steps.action: Opens an address inside the app, such as a project page, while signed out, or opens Sign in from the landing page.
Sends a signed-out person to Sign in and remembers the address they asked for.
Enters Email and Password and presses Sign in, or clicks one of the five cards under Or continue with a sample account.
Checks that the email and password match an account in this browser and signs the person in.
Opens the page they asked for, or their home page (/app/home) if there was none.

rules: An empty field, or an email that does not look like an email address, is flagged under the field before anything is checked.
A wrong email or a wrong password shows the same message, That email and password do not match, so the page never reveals which accounts exist.
Remember me on this device is ticked by default. Unticked, closing the browser signs the person out. The sample account cards always remember.

The five cards are Priya Nair (Architect, Studio Oriel), Isla Brennan (Client (developer), Lantern Quay Developments), Tom Ashby (Donor building owner, Ostlea Estates), Dana Kowalski (Site surveyor, Tarnbrook Deconstruction) and Marcus Lindqvist (Sustainability consultant, Halewick Sustainability). Every sample account uses the password sandbox.
A sample card signs in with the password sandbox. If someone has changed that account's password on Reset your password, the card fails with the mismatch message until the sandbox is reset.

The remembered address is only ever a page inside the app on this site; anything else is ignored and the person goes to their home page. Opening /app or /app/home while signed out leads to a plain Sign in.
A person who opens Sign in, Create your account or Reset your password while already signed in goes straight on to the app.
Sign out is in the avatar menu. It shows You are signed out and opens a plain Sign in page, without offering the page they left.
Signing in only opens the door: each page still checks what this person may see (see Pages you may not open).

workflows.title: Create an account and an organisation
workflows.where: Create your account (/signup), from the Create an account link on Sign in
workflows.summary: A new person creates their own account and a new organisation in two steps. The organisation type they choose decides which workspace they get: architect, client, donor building owner, surveyor or sustainability consultant.
workflows.mermaid:
flowchart TD
A["Enters full name, work email, password"] --> B["Presses Continue"]
B --> C{"Details filled in correctly?"}:::system
C -->|"No"| D(["Field errors shown"]):::system
C -->|"Yes"| E["Enters organisation name"]
E --> F["Chooses organisation type"]
F --> G["Presses Create account"]
G --> H{"Email already has an account?"}:::system
H -->|"Yes"| I(["Told to sign in instead"]):::system
H -->|"No"| J["Account and organisation created"]:::system
J --> K["Signed in"]:::system
K --> L(["Home opens with a welcome message"])

steps.action: On Step 1 of 2 enters Full name, Work email and Password, then presses Continue.
Checks the three fields and, if they are fine, moves to Step 2 of 2, Your organisation.
Enters Organisation name, picks one Organisation type card, then presses Create account.
Checks every field again, including whether the email already has an account, then creates the organisation and the person and signs them in.
Opens home and shows the message Welcome to (organisation name), Your workspace is ready.

rules: The five organisation types are Architecture practice, Developer or client, Donor building owner, Surveying or deconstruction firm, and Sustainability consultancy. Architecture practice is selected until the person picks another.
The password needs at least 8 characters. The email must look like an email address, for example name@company.example. The organisation name cannot be left empty.
Whether the email is already in use is only checked on Create account. If it is, step 2 shows An account with this email already exists. Sign in instead.
The organisation type cannot be changed later: Settings, Organisation says it sets the workspace and cannot be changed.
A new organisation starts empty; the new person is its only member until they invite colleagues.
Back on step 2 returns to step 1 without losing what was typed.
The new person stays signed in on this device after closing the browser.
notifications: None. The welcome is an on-screen message only.

workflows.title: First visit to a new workspace
workflows.summary: A new organisation has no records, so each home page opens with a first step suited to its type. The architect is walked into creating a first project; the others see an empty home that says what to do or what to wait for.
workflows.mermaid:
flowchart TD
A["New account lands on home"]:::system --> B{"Which organisation type?"}:::system
B -->|"Architect"| C["Create your first project dialog opens"]:::system
C --> D{"Creates the project now?"}:::arch
D -->|"Yes"| E(["New project page opens"]):::arch
D -->|"No, closes it"| F(["Welcome card with three steps"]):::arch
B -->|"Owner"| G(["Add your first building"]):::owner
B -->|"Surveyor"| H(["No appointments yet, Add building"]):::surveyor
B -->|"Client"| I(["Wait for a project request"]):::client
B -->|"Consultant"| J(["Wait to be added to a project"]):::consultant

steps.action: Opens home for the new organisation's workspace.
Sees the Create your first project dialog open at once. Creating the project opens its page; closing the dialog leaves the Welcome to your workspace card.
On the Welcome card can press Create a project or Browse the Marketplace, beside three steps: Create your first project, Find materials in the Marketplace, Send your shortlist for approval.
Sees Add your first building and Building something too?, each with a button (Add building, Add new project) that opens the Buildings page with the add dialog.
Sees No appointments yet with an Add building button to start capturing straight away.
Sees No projects yet: a project appears once an architect asks to add the organisation as client and the client accepts under Project requests.
Sees No projects yet and No engagements: a project appears when an architect adds the consultancy to it.

rules: The dialog opens by itself only for an architect, and only on the visit straight after Create account. A person who joins through an invite does not get it.
The architect's Welcome card stays until the organisation has a project; then the normal dashboard takes its place.
Client and consultant workspaces cannot start a project themselves; they are brought in by an architect.
notifications: None. The on-screen message reads Welcome to (organisation name), Your workspace is ready.

workflows.title: Reset a forgotten password in the sandbox
workflows.where: Reset your password (/forgot-password), from Forgot password? on Sign in
workflows.summary: In the sandbox no email is sent, so the person sets a new password on the page itself and is signed in straight away. The page says plainly that a live service would email a link instead.
workflows.mermaid:
flowchart TD
A["Clicks Forgot password on Sign in"] --> B["Enters email and new password twice"]
B --> C["Presses Reset password"]
C --> D{"Fields filled in correctly?"}:::system
D -->|"No"| E(["Field errors shown"]):::system
D -->|"Yes"| F{"Account exists for that email?"}:::system
F -->|"No"| G(["We could not find an account"]):::system
F -->|"Yes"| H["New password saved"]:::system
H --> I["Signed in, not remembered"]:::system
I --> J(["Home opens, Password updated"])

steps.action: Clicks Forgot password? beside the Password field on Sign in.
Enters Email, New password and Confirm new password, then presses Reset password.
Checks the fields, checks an account exists for that email, and saves the new password.
Signs the person in, opens home and shows Password updated, You are signed in with your new password.

rules: The page shows: In the sandbox you reset your password on this page. A live service would email you a link instead.
Anyone who types an account's email can set its password here; nothing checks that the email is theirs. This is a sandbox shortcut.
An unknown email is refused with We could not find an account with that email.
The new password needs at least 8 characters and both entries must match (The two passwords do not match).
After a reset the sign-in is not remembered: closing the browser signs the person out.

Any account can be reset this way, including the sample accounts. A sample account with a changed password can no longer use its one-click card on Sign in; Reset the sandbox puts the password back to sandbox.
Back to sign in returns to Sign in without changing anything.

workflows.title: Invite a teammate
workflows.where: Settings, Team (/app/settings/team), from Settings in the sidebar or the avatar menu
workflows.summary: Any member invites a colleague into their own organisation by email address. The sandbox sends no email: it makes an invite link and copies it, ready to pass on.
workflows.mermaid:
flowchart TD
A["Opens Settings, Team"] --> B["Enters the colleague email address"]
B --> C["Presses Create invite"]
C --> D{"Email valid, free and not invited?"}:::system
D -->|"No"| E(["Reason shown under the field"]):::system
D -->|"Yes"| F["Invite link made and copied"]:::system
F --> G["Passes the link to the colleague"]
G --> H{"Change of mind?"}
H -->|"Yes"| I["Presses Revoke"]
I --> J(["Link stops working, Undo offered"]):::system
H -->|"No"| K(["Waits under Pending invites"])

steps.action: Opens Settings, then Team, and types the colleague's address under Invite a colleague.
Presses Create invite.
Makes an invite link, copies it and shows Invite created. Link copied.
Passes the link on; Copy link beside the invite under Pending invites copies it again.
May press Revoke on a pending invite; the message Invite revoked offers Undo.

rules: Anyone in the organisation can invite and revoke; there is no separate admin.
The invite is always into the inviter's own organisation, so the colleague gets the same workspace type.

Refused with a reason under the field: Enter a valid email address; This person is already a member; Another account already uses this email (someone in another organisation); This person already has a pending invite.
No email is sent. If the browser blocks copying, the link is shown in a message to copy by hand.
Because all sandbox data stays in one browser, the link only works when it is opened in this same browser. Opened anywhere else it shows This invite link is not valid.
Pending invites shows each email, its link, how long ago it was sent and by whom. Accepted and revoked invites drop off the list.
Members lists everyone in the organisation with the date they joined.
notifications: None when the invite is made or revoked. When it is accepted, see Accept an invite.
workflows.states_mermaid:
stateDiagram-v2
[*] --> Pending : Create invite
Pending --> Accepted : Colleague joins
Pending --> Revoked : Revoke
Revoked --> Pending : Undo
Accepted --> [*]
Revoked --> [*]
workflows.states_note: Only a pending invite link works. Undo after Revoke works only while nothing else has changed since.

workflows.title: Accept an invite and join the team
workflows.where: Join your team (/invite/:token), opened from the invite link
workflows.summary: The invited person opens the link, sees who invited them and to which organisation, and creates their account with a name and password. They join that organisation and land in its workspace.
workflows.mermaid:
flowchart TD
A["Opens the invite link"] --> B{"Invite still pending?"}:::system
B -->|"No"| C(["This invite link is not valid"]):::system
B -->|"Yes"| D["Sees organisation, inviter and type"]
D --> E["Enters full name and password"]
E --> F["Presses Join with the organisation name"]
F --> G{"Name, password and email all fine?"}:::system
G -->|"No"| H(["Error shown"]):::system
G -->|"Yes"| I["Joins the inviting organisation"]:::system
I --> J["Organisation members are notified"]:::system
J --> K(["Signed in, home opens"])

steps.action: Opens the link and sees Join (organisation name), who invited them, and the organisation type.
Keeps the email shown (it cannot be changed), enters Full name and Password, and presses the Join (organisation name) button.
Creates the person in the inviting organisation, marks the invite accepted and signs them in on this device.
Notifies the organisation that the person joined, opens home and shows Welcome to (organisation name), You have joined the team.

rules: The email is fixed to the address the invite was sent to.
A link that was never issued in this browser, already used or revoked shows This invite link is not valid, with Go to sign in.
If an account with that email was created meanwhile, joining is refused with An account with this email already exists. Sign in instead.
The name cannot be empty and the password needs at least 8 characters.
Someone already signed in who opens the link is warned that joining creates a new account for the invited email and signs them in with it.
The new member gets the organisation's workspace and sees what the organisation sees; there are no separate permissions for each person inside an organisation.
Already have an account? Sign in leads to Sign in instead.
notifications: The organisation gets one notification for its members: (name) joined (organisation name), They accepted the invite sent to (email). It links to Settings, Team. The person who joined sees it already read. A member who has turned off Team and projects in Settings, Notifications does not see it.

workflows.title: Switch between sample accounts
workflows.where: Avatar menu, Switch account (top bar); or Settings, Sandbox (/app/settings/sandbox)
workflows.summary: To follow a material from one side of the platform to the other, a person jumps straight into another sample account without typing a password. This exists only in the sandbox.
workflows.mermaid:
flowchart TD
A["Opens avatar menu, Switch account"] --> C["Picks another sample account"]
B["Opens Settings, Sandbox"] --> X["Presses Switch beside an account"]
C --> D["Signed in as that person"]:::system
X --> D
D --> E(["Their home opens, Signed in as shown"])

steps.action: Opens the avatar menu in the top bar and points at Switch account, or opens Settings, Sandbox.
Picks one of the accounts under Sample accounts in this sandbox, or presses Switch beside it in Settings.
Signs in as that person without a password, opens their home and shows Signed in as (name).

rules: Only the five sample accounts are listed. Accounts people created themselves never appear, so they cannot be switched to.
The current account shows a tick in the menu, or a Signed in badge in Settings, and cannot be picked.
Anyone signed in can switch, including someone using an account they created. To get back to that account they sign in with its email and password.
Switching keeps the same Remember me choice as the sign-in it replaces.

workflows.title: Reset the sandbox
workflows.where: Settings, Sandbox (/app/settings/sandbox), also reached from the Sandbox badge in the top bar
workflows.summary: Puts every sample record and photo back as it was at the start, wiping all changes made in this browser. It is used to rehearse a demo again from a clean start.
workflows.mermaid:
flowchart TD
A["Opens Settings, Sandbox"] --> B["Presses Reset"]
B --> C{"Confirm in the dialog?"}
C -->|"Cancel"| D(["Nothing changes"])
C -->|"Reset sandbox"| E["Sample records and photos restored"]:::system
E --> F{"Signed in with a sample account?"}:::system
F -->|"Yes"| G(["Home opens, Sandbox reset"]):::system
F -->|"No"| H["Own account removed, signed out"]:::system
H --> I(["Sign in opens"]):::system

steps.action: Opens Settings, Sandbox, and presses Reset under Reset the sandbox.
Confirms with Reset sandbox in the dialog Reset the sandbox?, or presses Cancel.
Clears stored photos and puts all sample data back, including the sample accounts and their notifications.
Shows Sandbox reset, Every sample record is back as it started, and opens home. A person whose own account no longer exists is signed out and sees Sign in.

rules: Anyone signed in can reset. The dialog warns that all changes made in this browser are lost: captures, listings, decisions, reservations and new accounts.
Accounts people created, their organisations and their invites are removed. Someone signed in with one is signed out.
Sample account passwords go back to sandbox.
The sample story is dated again from the day of the reset, so its dates move with it.
It affects only this browser; there is no server and nothing is sent anywhere.
There is no undo for a reset.
notifications: Notifications go back to the sample set; nobody is told of the reset.

workflows.title: Pages you may not open, and pages that do not exist
workflows.where: Any address; inside the app the page shows within the sidebar and top bar
workflows.summary: Every address inside the app is checked against the person's workspace and records before the page appears. A page they may not open shows a calm no-access page, and an address that does not exist shows Page not found; neither reveals anything about the record behind it.
workflows.mermaid:
flowchart TD
A["Opens an address"] --> B{"Inside the app?"}:::system
B -->|"No"| C{"Known public page?"}:::system
C -->|"Yes"| D(["Page opens"])
C -->|"No"| E(["Error 404, Page not found"]):::system
B -->|"Yes"| F{"Signed in?"}:::system
F -->|"No"| G["Signs in first"]
G --> H
F -->|"Yes"| H{"Is it a known page?"}:::system
H -->|"No"| I(["Page not found, Go to home"]):::system
H -->|"Yes"| J{"Allowed for this person?"}:::system
J -->|"Yes"| K(["Page opens"])
J -->|"No"| L(["You do not have access to this"]):::system

steps.action: Opens an address, for example from a link, a notification or a bookmark.
If the address is inside the app and the person is signed out, sends them to Sign in first and brings them back afterwards.
Checks that the page exists and that this person's workspace, organisation and records allow it.
Shows the page, or You do not have access to this, or Page not found, each with Go to home.

rules: Home, Notifications, Settings and Help open for everyone signed in.

Workspace pages are tied to the organisation type: Saved and New project are for architects; Buildings and Capture for owners and surveyors; Requests for owners; Project requests for clients; Engagements for consultants.

The Projects list and the Marketplace open for architects, clients and consultants, and for a donor building owner who is the client of a new project. A single material opens only if that person may see its listing.

A project opens only for organisations on it. A building opens only for its owner, its surveyor or its deconstruction contractor. Inside a building, Inventory, Capture and Testing are for the owner and the surveyor; Priorities, Listings and Sharing for the owner; Availability for the contractor.
An address for a project or building that does not exist shows the no-access page, the same as one the person may not open, so nobody can tell which records exist.
The no-access page says the page belongs to another workspace or organisation and to ask the person who sent the link. It never shows the record's name or any figure.
Old addresses still work: /app/discover goes to the Marketplace and a project's carbon tab goes to Sustainability.
If a page fails to load, the app shows Something went wrong inside the sidebar and top bar, suggesting a sandbox reset if it keeps happening.
Outside the app, an unknown address shows Error 404 with Go to home, back to the landing page.

workflows.title: Search with Ctrl K or Cmd K
workflows.where: Anywhere inside the app: Search in the top bar, or Ctrl K (Cmd K on a Mac)
workflows.summary: A search box over everything the person may open: pages, projects, buildings, inventory items and materials. Choosing a result goes straight to it.
workflows.mermaid:
flowchart TD
A["Presses Ctrl K or Search"] --> B["Search box opens"]:::system
B --> C["Types a few words"]
C --> D["Looks only in what person may open"]:::system
D --> E{"Anything matches?"}:::system
E -->|"No"| F(["Nothing matches that"]):::system
E -->|"Yes"| G["Picks a result"]
G --> H(["That page opens"])

steps.action: Presses Ctrl K, or Cmd K on a Mac, or clicks Search in the top bar.
Opens the box Search materials, projects and pages; before typing it lists the person's pages, projects and buildings.
Types words; results are grouped as Pages, Projects, Buildings, Materials and Inventory.
Picks a result to open it, or presses the shortcut again or Escape to close.

rules: Results come only from what the person may open: their workspace's pages and Notifications, the projects their organisation is on, and the buildings their organisation owns, surveys or dates as contractor, with those buildings' inventory items.
A deconstruction contractor's inventory results open the no-access page, because a contractor alone may not open a building's inventory.

Materials are searched only by architects, clients, consultants, and donor building owners who are the client of a new project. They come from public listings, listings shared with them, and materials already reserved for their projects.
A material result shows its picture, family and location; nothing private about the seller is searchable.
Every word typed must match. Results whose name starts with what was typed come first. At most 24 results show.
The shortcut works even while typing in a field, but only inside the app, not on the sign-in pages.

workflows.title: Undo a change
workflows.where: The message that appears at the bottom of the screen after a change, across the app
workflows.summary: Many changes, such as saving a material, revoking an invite or changing a notification setting, show a short message with an Undo button. Pressing it puts everything back as it was just before that change.
workflows.mermaid:
flowchart TD
A["Person makes a change"] --> B["Message with Undo appears"]:::system
B --> C{"Presses Undo in time?"}
C -->|"No"| D(["Change stays"])
C -->|"Yes"| E{"Anything else changed since?"}:::system
E -->|"Yes"| F(["Nothing happens"]):::system
E -->|"No"| G(["Back as it was before"]):::system

steps.action: Makes a change, for example Revoke on an invite.
Shows a message with Undo for about eight seconds.
Presses Undo.
Puts the data back exactly as it was before that change, including removing any notification the change sent.

rules: Undo works only while nothing else has changed since, so it never throws away later work by anyone in this browser. If something has changed, pressing Undo does nothing and no message explains why.
Undo is offered only in the message after the change; it is lost once the message goes or the page reloads.
Not everything has Undo: for example signing in, creating an account, creating an invite, switching account and resetting the sandbox do not.
There is no keyboard shortcut for undo.
notifications: A notification created by the change is removed again by the undo.
